inference.made_by: backup/where-the-return-lands.py, backup/the-balance-the-effect-prints.py, backup/publish-the-balance-sweep.py, backup/where-the-balance-knees-are.py, backup/publish-the-balance-knees.py, backup/a-voice-whose-tail-has-gone.py, backup/whether-the-corner-is-this-types.py, backup/write-the-balance-inference.py

claim: A byte printed `D> 0E - D 0<E` is two multipliers, each of them the byte's distance from a corner divided by fifty, truncated onto a grid of a hundred and twenty-eight and clamped at both ends -- and the two are offset so that they meet at full rather than crossing. The half that goes past the effect holds at its dry-end level for every setting up to and including 64, leaves it at 65, and is at nothing from 114 on. Read every count over both corners, thirty-two settings land within a sixth of a step of `min(1, floor((114 - n) * 128 / 50) / 128)` on the ramp and within half a step anywhere, and each of the three numbers in it is pinned by the reading: a quarter of a count on the width costs six times the residual, rounding instead of truncating costs seven times it, and the multipliers sit a twelfth of a step from the grid's entries where a number on no grid would sit a quarter of one away. Read in the window the return arrives in, the effect's own half rises for the last time at 64 and holds from 65, ten times what the takes repeat either way, so it is the direct half reflected through 128 rather than through 127: `min(1, floor((n - 14) * 128 / 50) / 128)`, whose corner and the direct half's sum to 128, and which meets the direct half at full at exactly 64. That half is read on two of the three types and carried by a shape rather than a threshold: truncation makes the four steps over the corner uneven, and reflected through 128 they are predicted at 0.220, 0.144, 0.211 and 0.206 of a decibel and read within 0.010 of that on one type and 0.031 on the other, where reflecting through 127 is out by 0.200 and 0.175. So the middle of the byte carries both halves at once and stands three decibels over either end, which is the opposite sign to a crossfade and not flat. Both ends reach true nothing: the direct window at the effect end falls to 1.1 decibels over the same take's own lead, which is the interface and not the unit. The law was found on one type at one count and holds on the two others, read at eight counts on a different day, to seven tenths of a step.
named: min(1, floor((114 - n) * 128 / 50) / 128) past the effect and min(1, floor((n - 14) * 128 / 50) / 128) through it, which is the same law reflected through 128 rather than through 127, so the two meet at full at 64
why_it_can_be_named: The sweep read this byte every eight counts and left a shape that was read off it afterwards, which is a readout and not a name. What makes it a name is that the readout was written down as a prediction -- corners sharp within one count, at 64 and at 114 -- and then read at one count, where it could have failed and did not. Three things came back that the sweep could not have arranged: both corners are sharp, the width is fifty counts and not forty-nine and three quarters or fifty and a quarter, and the multipliers sit on a grid. None of the three is a free parameter fitted per setting; the whole law is three numbers against thirty-two readings, and a fourteen-setting run of alternating step sizes that no straight line predicts and a truncated one does. The one place the prediction was wrong is the offset of the effect's half, and it was wrong by one count in a direction the same run settled: the readout reflected the law through 127 and the effect half was measured still rising at 64, which with the width and the grid already pinned leaves 14 and no other offset. That is the shape being corrected against a reading rather than carried, and it is why the two halves are exact mirrors and 0 is the byte value with no partner.
could_have_been_refuted_by: The catalogue's five candidates each named a figure at the centre of the byte and a figure at the ends, and the run returned both: a dry half 3.01 decibels down at the centre would have carried the constant-power pair, 6.02 the crossfade, 2.44 the pan table, and a bottom stopping twenty-five decibels short of the lead would have carried the pan table on its other prediction. None came back. Then the shape left standing made three predictions of its own and was read at six times the resolution: a corner rounded over as little as two counts would have shown the settings either side of 64 leaving the clamp early and in one direction, a width off by a quarter of a count would have shown a whole step of error, and multipliers not on a grid would have sat a quarter of a step from every entry. All three could have happened and none did.

measurements.why: The byte at nineteen settings on one type and nine on two others, each type's front half held and its output stage left flat, read in three windows of one length whose places were measured in each type's own first two takes. The direct sound's window is the reading the claim rests on: it repeats to two hundredths of a decibel on every type and carries no part of the effect's return at all.

Every count from 56 to 72 and from 108 to 120, on the type whose takes repeat best, with the same block held and the windows found the same way. This is the run the shape could have failed in: eight counts between settings cannot tell a sharp corner from a rounded one or see a step pattern at all, and one count does both. The direct window carries the law; the late window carries only which neighbouring pair still differs, which is all the effect half's corner needs and all the tail leaves readable there.

Every count from 60 to 68 on a second type, four takes each, asked for by this claim's own queue. The type was chosen by how well its late window repeats rather than by how deep its tail is, because a step is a difference between neighbours and the tail is common to them -- 01 50's tail is six decibels shallower than 01 57's and it reads this just as well. 01 54 is left out by the same test and not by its tail: its late window does not repeat at all.

era_priors.claim: A pair of multipliers worked out once by the control processor when the byte is written, not per sample. Two clamped straight lines are two subtractions and two comparisons, which is cheaper than the table this class expected and cheaper than the two the machine already carries.
era_priors.why: The same reasoning the effect level and the output pan were read under, and the reason this class expected a third table. What the measurement says is that the designer did not reuse either one, and did not store a third: a shape a straight line reproduces to a quarter of one percent over fifty settings is not a stored curve.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: The multipliers did not land on a straight line -- a stored table is free to curve and would, anywhere its designer wanted a taper.

era_priors.claim: Both halves at full in the middle is a choice rather than an accident. It keeps the two ends at the level a bypass would give and removes the three-decibel dip a crossfade has in the middle, at the cost of three decibels of headroom there.
era_priors.why: An insertion effect on a part has to sound the same level with the effect off as with it on, or every patch that uses one has to be re-levelled. A crossfade does not give that; this does.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: The two ends did not come back at the same level as each other. They do not on two of the three types, and the reason is the effect's own return level rather than the balance -- which is why the claim is about each half's shape and not about the total.

adds: The record says what each setting of the byte did to the two windows of one take. What is added here is that the two windows are the two halves of the mix, that each half is a straight line in amplitude with a clamp at either end, and that the two lines do not cross -- they meet at full. None of that is in the record, which does not name a window dry or wet and does not fit anything.

alternatives.reading: The two ramps are one stored table per half, of a hundred and twenty-eight entries, that happens to be straight over its moving part and rounds off where it meets each clamp.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: Every count read over both corners. A table that rounds a corner leaves the clamp early and in one direction; measured, all nine settings from 56 to 64 sit at the dry end's own level to within what the takes repeat, 65 is already a full step down and on the line, 113 is one step over nothing and 114 is at nothing. Half of the alternative survives and is now the claim: the multipliers are on a grid, which is what a table would give -- what is refuted is a table free to hold any shape, because the entries are a truncated straight line and nothing else.

alternatives.reading: The ramps are forty parts in a hundred of the printed travel meeting at half of it, putting the corners at 12.7, 63.5 and 114.3, rather than fifty counts meeting at 64.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: The same run. Against the settings strictly inside the ramp the width of fifty and the corner at 114 are out by a sixth of a step at worst and the percentage reading by 1.17 steps, and a quarter of a count either way on the width costs a whole step. What the sweep could not separate, six times the resolution does.

alternatives.reading: The grid is a hundred and twenty-seven rather than a hundred and twenty-eight.

separated_by.why_not_separable: The two sit 0.0834 and 0.0854 of a step from their nearest entries over the same fourteen readings, which is a difference of two thousandths of a step against readings that scatter by a tenth of one. Every entry the two disagree about differs by less than the takes repeat, and reading more settings does not help because the disagreement is proportional and smallest where the readings are best. Recorded as equivalent rather than deferred. What the claim rests on is that there is a grid at all and that the multipliers are truncated onto it, and both readings give that.

alternatives.reading: The effect half is the direct half reflected through 127, reaching full at 63, rather than through 128, reaching full at 64. One step of the grid.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: The late window of the same one-count run, which the claim had put aside as too shallow to read. It is too shallow to read a level: the direct sound's own tail sits twenty-four decibels under the return, which moves an absolute figure by half a decibel. It is not too shallow for this. The direct half is clamped at full for every setting up to 64, so the tail is the same term at all of them and shifts them together; what is read is which neighbouring pair still differs, and no assumption about how the two add can change that. The effect half rises 0.20 of a decibel from 63 to 64 and 0.00 from 64 to 65, each ten times what those takes repeat. With the width at fifty counts and the grid at 128, already pinned by the direct half, `floor((64 - s) * 128 / 50) >= 128` and `floor((63 - s) * 128 / 50) < 128` leave s = 14 and nothing else. The eight-minute run this alternative had queued is not needed, and the probe written for it says it could not have been made: seven voices were read for how much of themselves they leave in the late window and the deepest reached 33.2 decibels against a bar of 40.

alternatives.reading: The offset of 14 is this type's and not the class's. The direct half is read on three types and agrees on all three; the effect half's corner is read on one.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: The run it asked for, made on 01 50 with nothing changed but the settings and the type. It rises 0.175 of a decibel from 63 to 64 and 0.000 from 64 to 65, against takes repeating to 0.03 -- the same corner 01 57 gives. What the run returned beyond that was not asked for and is the stronger half of it: truncation makes the steps over the corner uneven, and the four of them are a shape rather than a threshold. Reflected through 128 they are predicted at 0.220, 0.144, 0.211 and 0.206 of a decibel and read at 0.210, 0.130, 0.205 and 0.175, worst disagreement 0.031; reflected through 127 the same four are predicted at 0.144, 0.211, 0.206 and 0.000 and the worst disagreement is 0.175. On 01 57 the two come to 0.010 and 0.200. So the offset is the class's on both types this can be read on, and it is carried by a run of four predicted step sizes and not by one step being present.

alternatives.reading: The law is the same law on the forty-three types this reading cannot reach, whose return is not a copy of the note arriving later.

separated_by.why_not_separable: Not by this reading, on any type. What it needs is a window holding one half and not the other, and those types do not give one: a chorus, a filter and a compressor all return something that begins while the note is still sounding. The byte sits four places ahead of a tail already read as one structure shared across types, which makes one shared balance the thing to expect rather than the thing to assume, and three delays agreeing is three types agreeing and not forty-six. What could carry it is the tail argument read off other records, which is a different claim and not a run.

refuted_by: A setting of this byte on any of these types whose direct window lands more than one step of the grid from `min(1, floor((114 - n) * 128 / 50) / 128)` times its own reading at the dry end. In particular any reading between 56 and 64 that is not level with the reading at 0, any reading between 114 and 127 that has not gone to the take's own lead, or a run of settings on the ramp whose steps do not alternate between two sizes -- a straight line that is not truncated steps evenly. On the effect's own half, a late window that does not rise from 63 to 64, or that rises again after 64, on any type whose return arrives clear of the note.

reproduces.domain: The byte at nineteen settings on 01 54 and nine each on 01 50 and 01 57, read as the level in each of two windows of one take and as the two together, and then at every count from 56 to 72 and 108 to 120 on 01 57, and at every count from 60 to 68 on 01 50.

compared_against.why_not_a_filter: An arrival record holds one run per directory of takes and carries no type on the run itself, so there is no field an index query could select on. The three runs are the whole of the record and naming them is naming it.

residual.read_as: the multiplier, in steps of the grid it lands on
residual.why: The direct half against three numbers -- a corner, a width and a grid -- with no entry per setting anywhere in it. Reported in steps of the grid rather than in decibels because a step is what the law can be wrong by: a share of full scale would be a number nothing here is quantised in. The first figure is the run that read every count, the second the worst any of the three types gives. The effect half's residual is larger and is reported per type below, because on one of the three it is the take's own repeat scatter and not a departure from the law.

which_grid_the_multipliers_land_on.read_as: how far each multiplier sits from the nearest entry, as a share of one step

01-57.read_as: the level in the window the return arrives in, one count at a time
01-57.why_the_tail_does_not_reach_this: The direct half is clamped at full for every setting up to 64, so whatever of the note is still sounding in the late window is the same term at all of them. It shifts every reading in the range together and cannot make one neighbouring pair differ where another does not, which is the whole of what is read here.

with_the_tail_taken_away.why_it_does_not_carry_the_finding: How far the tail and the return correlate is not known and is solved for, and which offset the recovered ramp prefers moves with it: nothing correlated gives 12, half gives 14, wholly correlated gives 15. Reported because at the correlation the clamped settings actually return it agrees with the corner, and it would have been worth knowing if it had not.

reproduces.why_the_wet_half_is_read_apart: 01 54 is a delay whose time is modulated, and its late window does not repeat: four takes of one setting spread 3.1 decibels and every pair splits the same way round, the first take of a setting reading 1.35 decibels over the second. The return walks in and out of a window that does not move. Its direct window repeats to a hundredth of a decibel over the same takes, which is why the claim is carried by the direct window and the other two types carry the wet half.

what_this_does_not_close.what: Whether the knees are sharp or rounded over a few counts.
what_this_does_not_close.bounded_by: The sweep's own spacing. Eight counts between settings on the densest type, so a knee up to seven counts wide would read as sharp.

what_this_does_not_close.what: Where the effect half leaves nothing, which the law puts at 14 and no reading has been made at.
what_this_does_not_close.bounded_by: The tail, and this time it does bound it. At that end the effect half is a step or two of the grid, thirty-six decibels under its own full -- and the direct sound's tail in the same window is twenty-four decibels under it, so the thing to be read sits twelve decibels beneath what it would be read through. Seven voices were tried for a shallower tail and the deepest reached 33.2 decibels against a bar of 40, so no gated note on this unit reaches it either. The offset of 14 is where the corner at 64, the width and the grid put it, not somewhere a reading has been taken.

what_this_does_not_close.what: Whether the byte value with no partner is 0 because the table is written that way or because the two halves are computed and 0 falls out.
what_this_does_not_close.bounded_by: Not separable by any reading of the output. The two halves are exact mirrors under n -> 128 - n, which maps 1 to 127 and 64 to itself and leaves 0 unpaired; that is a fact about the law and the same numbers come out either way it is arrived at.

what_this_does_not_close.what: Whether the part panpot's balance and this one are the same byte.
what_this_does_not_close.bounded_by: Not asked. Nothing in this run touched a part, and the address swept is the effect's own.

what_this_does_not_close.what: What the law is on the types whose return overlaps the note -- a reverb, a chorus, a filter, a compressor.
what_this_does_not_close.bounded_by: Named and refused rather than measured. A reverb's return was measured to begin a tenth of a second after the note, inside it, so this reading has no window there and says nothing about those rows.

what_it_would_change: Sixty-five rows over forty-six types stop being unknown as a shape. Three of them are now read; the rest are read as the same shape only as far as the tail argument carries, which is a reading of other records and not of this one. What changes for a renderer is that the middle of this byte is not a mix at all -- putting a part's effect balance at 64 asks for both halves at full and three decibels more output than either end, and a renderer that crossfaded there would be six decibels light on the dry half at that setting.
